    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online.

    The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump.

    After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.

    “Thank you all for the second chance,” he mentioned. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”.

    Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”.

    Sources indicate that amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Times reported that Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa.
    • In a recent development, the Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa’s governor-elect, who won’t be sworn into office until January.

    In a recent development, the Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP).

    Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation.

    It has been revealed that late Thursday, a federal appeals court granted Earthjustice’s request to put a hold on the Army’s permit from the Environmental Protection Agency, which allowed for the controlled detonation to be carried out. Around the same time, Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said the detonation would be postponed until Monday so the military could communicate with Iowans about the situation and plans.

    Documents released by the Army last week remarked that the military first learned in March that the lead azide had started to degrade and crystallize. Lead azide is used in detonators for munitions, but in crystallized form it becomes highly unstable and sensitive to physical movement or friction. The IAAAP is said to contain around 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of lead azide in barrels held in earth-covered containers.

    It has been revealed that in late March, the Army awarded a contract to MuniRem Environmental, a Georgia-based firm that uses chemicals to neutralize munitions to safely dispose of the lead azide, according to a Fresh York Times report. MuniRem uses a sulfur-based solution that reportedly breaks down explosives and immobilizes toxic chemicals, eliminating the need for detonation. The manufacturer had proposed spraying the inside of the earth-covered containers housing the barrels as well as the barrel surfaces to neutralize risks of spontaneous explosions.

    But two months later, the Army canceled the contract without explanation. An Army contracting officer told MuniRem in an email at the time that the cancellation “was not based on deficiencies” in MuniRem’s plans, the Times reported. The tech giant’s founder noted MuniRem filed public records requests to get more information on why the contract was scrapped, but it has not received a response.

    Now, the Army claims that the lead azide has only degraded further since March and it cannot move the barrels or even open their lids without risking a catastrophic explosion. Further, it claims that winter temperatures in the coming days increase the risk of spontaneous detonation.

    It has been revealed that “As the temperatures drop, the risk of an uncontrolled explosion increases because the formed crystals can break more easily in freezing temperatures,” lawyers for the Trump administration wrote in a court filing over the weekend. “If the crystals break, this could cause a chain reaction detonation that could cause an uncontrolled dispersal of lead azide into the environment.”.

    According to recent reports, the Army claims that the only choice now is between a controlled, mitigated explosion or an uncontrolled, unmitigated explosion. In court filings this weekend, government lawyers argued that the Army does not need the now-suspended EPA permit to move forward with the detonation, because the Army has determined that the lead azide poses an “immediate threat to human health, public safety, property, or the environment.”.

    Last Thursday, Telle said that the delay until Monday was the “latest possible moment” for a controlled detonation before temperatures dropped dangerously low. But the military subsequently delayed the detonation again until Tuesday and then pushed it back to Wednesday.

    In his social media post Monday, Trump said he thought carrying out the controlled detonation was the “proper course.” But he said he was making the decision the responsibility of the federal appeals court and Governor-elect Rob Sand, a Democrat. If the lead azide spontaneously detonates on their watch, Trump claimed, they will be fully to blame.

    “If he or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation,” Trump wrote.

    In a social media post Sunday evening, Sand called for answers on how the situation was able to become so dangerous, specifically raising the question of why MuniRem’s contact was canceled.

    “Iowans deserve transparency over how we got here, then answers and accountability to stop this from ever happening again,” he wrote.

    #150268. The three DISM commands you should know to fix your Windows system images

    The three DISM commands you should know to fix your Windows system images

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Check and repair damaged system files with these DISM commands.
    • Your Windows installation depends on a collection of notable system files to run applications, install updates and perform everyday computing tasks.
    • DISM is a command line tool that can scan Windows system images for corrupt system files and attempt repairs.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Check and repair damaged system files with these DISM commands.

    Your Windows installation depends on a collection of notable system files to run applications, install updates and perform everyday computing tasks. If these files get damaged or go missing, your system may behave erratically. You may encounter system errors, features not working as expected, freezes or other unexpected behavior. Sometimes restarting your computer or running the usual troubleshooting steps aren't enough to restore damaged system files. For such cases, Windows provides a built-in repair utility called Deployment Image Servicing and Management (DISM).

    DISM is a command line tool that can scan Windows system images for corrupt system files and attempt repairs. Particularly, there are three useful DISM commands that achieve this purpose: CheckHealth, ScanHealth and RestoreHealth. You can run DISM commands in either the command prompt or the PowerShell, but both CLIs require administrator privileges to make system-level changes. It's worth noting that DISM exclusively scans and repairs system files; your personal files remain untouched.

    All three DISM commands in question follow a specific syntax that begins with DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image. The parts following "DISM" in the syntax are called command-line options. The /Online CLI option specifies DISM to take action on the currently running Windows installation, while /Cleanup-Image performs recovery operations on the selected installation.

    According to recent reports, the first command is DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth. It checks whether Windows has already flagged corrupt system files and whether the corruption is repairable. This is the first recommended step when investigating corrupt system files as it takes very little time to complete.

    Recent findings suggest that the next command is DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth and it works slightly differently from the CheckHealth command. Unlike CheckHealth, the ScanHealth DISM command performs a fresh scan of your system files and reports any its findings. The ScanHealth operation may take several minutes to complete, but it provides you with a fresh report on the component store's health.

    Recent findings suggest that finally, the DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth command both scans the component store for corruption and attempts to repair them automatically. By default, RestoreHealth uses Windows Update to obtain the necessary system files needed to repair the component store. The Windows component store is a protected internal repository that contains important system files. Windows requires these files to service, update and customize the operating system.

    Recent findings suggest that sometimes system file damage can also break Windows Enhancement, preventing DISM from downloading replacement files. When this happens, you can use an official Windows installation media to supply DISM with the necessary repair files. You can download a Windows ISO from Microsoft's official download page. Once downloaded, right click the ISO file and select mount. Windows will create a virtual drive for the ISO, assign it a drive letter and make its contents available.

    In a recent development, next, you'll need to check the Windows editions available in the downloaded installation media. You can do that by launching the command prompt as an administrator and running the DISM /Get-ImageInfo /ImageFile:D:sourcesinstall.wim command. This command lists the Windows editions available on the installation media along with their index numbers. Make a note of the index number corresponding to your installed edition before proceeding to the next step.

    Now, run the DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:WIM:D:sourcesinstall.wim:6 /LimitAccess command. Replace D: with the drive letter assigned to the mounted Windows ISO and 6 with the index number corresponding to your Windows edition. This directs DISM to use the installation media as its repair source instead of downloading files from Windows Revision.

    Once DISM completes its operation, run the sfc /scannow command to repair damaged or missing system files. Microsoft recommends running the DISM repair utility before System File Checker (SFC) because DISM repairs the Windows component store, which SFC relies on to replace corrupted system files.

    #150267. Breaking: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang

    Breaking: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2652 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.﻿.
    • Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.﻿.
    • In a recent development, after Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.﻿.

    Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.﻿.

    In a recent development, after Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump mentioned that Huang would “end up on his feet.”.

    “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.

    It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director.

    “There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump stated in a celebratory call to CNBC.

    Sources indicate that trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.

    “There’s nothing wrong with a comeback”.

    Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The Newly introduced York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday.

    News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.

    Sources indicate that trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he remarked on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.”.

    Sources indicate that but the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration.

    Sources indicate that the past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st.

    Sources indicate that the Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation.

    The board also mentioned it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the manufacturer and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added.

    Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The Fresh York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. But on Sunday evening, Trump still argued for Huang’s return and managed to continue flipping Nvidia’s board in his favor after a weekend’s worth of efforts.

    “[I]ndefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible”.

    Industry observers note that if the board maintained any hang-ups about bringing Huang back as CEO, Trump’s power over the executive branch — and the pressure he could exert with it — might have offered a compelling counterargument. The Securities and Exchange Commission had previously opened an investigation into whether Nvidia “misled investors,” according to The Wall Street Journal. But in a post on Truth Social Monday, Trump noted that the attorney general “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Reached for comment, the DOJ did not provide an on-the-record response in line with The Verge’s editorial policy.

    Key Democrats have indicated that both Nvidia and the Trump administration will be under fire when the newly introduced Congress is sworn in — and momentum has built behind GPU export controls, which Huang lobbied extensively to loosen. “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.” Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said in a post on X, adding they’d work “on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.” Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible” and pledged to investigate “business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.” He called for “traditional Republicans” to join in the effort.

    In a recent development, “The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the tech giant’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, mentioned in a statement. “Jensen Huang’s return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk.” Rep. Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, said, “A real Congress will find out” whether Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had any alternative incentives for their role in Nvidia’s dealings. Sen. Mark Warner, the top Democrat on the Intelligence Committee, called Trump’s intervention to bring back Huang “outrageous.” Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-TX), a member of the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs Committees, which are interviewing Huang next week, said he wants to know how Trump stands to benefit from “personally champion[ing] Huang’s return.”.

    “We need to know why Trump put his thumb on the scale to have Jensen reinstated as CEO”.

    Recent findings suggest that at closed-door hearings next week, Democrats say they intend to press Huang and the administration further, and several accused the administration of corruption. “We need to know why Trump put his thumb on the scale to have Jensen reinstated as CEO and why his administration failed to restrict the PRC’s access to our most sensitive technology,” Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said in a statement to The Verge. The board’s decision is “outrageous,” said Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a member of the House Select Committee on China. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” Krishnamoorthi said in a statement, calling for Huang to testify publicly. “Reinstatement is no substitute for accountability,” Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL), another China Committee member, said in a statement.

    California Attorney General Rob Bonta also intends to continue an investigation into the company. “The reinstatement of Jensen Huang does not change the fact that the American people deserve to know what happened here — whether Nvidia misled investors and the public,” California Department of Justice spokesperson Elissa Perez stated in a statement.

    In a recent development, last week, before Huang was reinstated, at least two Republican China hawks opposed the idea. Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO), a rumored potential presidential candidate, told reporters that he would not like to see Huang return to the top post, but would “defer to the board how they want to run their firm. If it were me and a guy who just was caught up in a Chinese honeytrap — I think is the technical term for it — I don’t think that I would impose massive security concerns, not just for the company, but for American national security.”.

    While it was up to the board to decide whether to bring Huang back, Hawley said, “We in Congress ought to be concerned about the American national security implications and I think we should be looking into that.”.

    Huang “has a serious credibility problem”.

    House China Committee Chair John Moolenaar (R-MI) stated on stage last week at the Aspen Cyber Summit in Washington, D.C., that Huang “has a serious credibility problem, and I don’t believe he would be as effective now as he was before.” His office did not immediately respond to a request for comment after Huang’s reinstatement.

    Sitting beside Moolenaar on stage last week, Rep. Greg Stanton (D-AZ) gave his advice to the board: “Don’t do it. Don’t bring it back. And at the very least, slow your roll, because there are so many questions that have to be answered. What else is out there that Jensen Huang has done to put US national security at risk?” Stanton warned that Congress is just beginning to probe what happened here. “There are going to be very serious investigations with very serious ramifications if in fact it is as it seems,” he stated. “The firm needs to know this ain’t going away for a while. This is a very serious problem.” After news of Huang’s return, Stanton doubled down on calls for investigations.

    Other Republicans — some of whom are leaving Congress — notably disagreed with Trump’s jubilance for Huang’s return. “It’s inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO,” retiring Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE) told CNBC. “To me it’s a failure of character.” Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE) wrote on X that Huang’s “behavior does not support reinstatement,” and said he must still testify before Congress. “It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips,” he wrote. Senate Intelligence Committee Chair Tom Cotton (R-AR) wrote on X that he’s not done investigating. “The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back,” he said. “Congress has much to investigate and we will pass overwhelmingly bipartisan chip export-control bills, including my Chip Security Act, one way or the other.”.

    “Congress has much to investigate”.

    Market analysts have been watching and waiting for a Huang comeback since reports that he had assembled a “war room” of allies to help with his possible reinstatement. Not only did Huang cofound one of the world’s most valuable companies and arguably the most notable one in the AI boom, but he has personally helped secure hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure funding from US financial institutions. Demand for Nvidia chips constantly outpaces supply, and Huang has had the president’s ear for months. Despite all that, though, Huang’s clout seemed like it wouldn’t help him up until the past 24 hours.

    Lindsey Stewart, director of institutional insights at Morningstar, wrote in a note that although investors may consider this a “good move given his history of value creation at the organization,” questions remain about the best way to provide corporate governance and oversight at such an important company.

    Jacob Bourne, an eMarketer analyst specializing in ad tech and consumer technologies, remarked in a statement to The Verge that it was difficult to gauge “how much protection Trump’s assurances will ultimately provide Nvidia.” And Heather West, head of Eurasia Group’s geo-technology practice, highlighted the fact that Trump recently met with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. The timing offers Democrats and China hawks “a great deal to work with in 2027 as they begin scrutiny into the administration, potential corruption, and large tech companies[‘] actions here,” said West.

    Analysts at Yorkville Ives wrote in a note Monday that they consider Nvidia a $300 stock with Huang and a $225 stock without him, due to his hard-to-replace influence in the sector. They said an interim structure “could not replicate” his supply relationships with TSMC and others, as well as his place in AI industry dealmaking.

    “This is a board that reversed itself because the alternative, a founder-less Nvidia at the start of the Rubin cycle with a CEO search running into next year, was the bigger risk to shareholders, and it chose to pair the reversal with the governance architecture investors will want to see around him,” the Yorkville Ives analysts wrote.

    Even Trump admits, though, that a true comeback story can’t be called in a single day. “I’ve seen some pretty good comebacks but I’ll tell you, what you have to have for a comeback, really, is longevity,” he told CNBC. He described the pep talk he gave Huang the night before. “I said, ‘You’ve got to promise me one thing. You’ve got the brain, you’ve got everything going, you’ve got to work hard. And if you work hard nobody can beat you.’”.

    According to Trump, Huang told him, “I’m going to work harder than I’ve ever worked.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Trump administration added Megaspeed International, the firm at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, to a trade blacklist on Monday.
    • That means that the Singapore-based firm will not be able to obtain US technology, including semiconductors, without obtaining a license from the US government.
    • The news was reported by Semafor, an American news website.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Trump administration added Megaspeed International, the firm at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, to a trade blacklist on Monday.

    That means that the Singapore-based firm will not be able to obtain US technology, including semiconductors, without obtaining a license from the US government.

    The news was reported by Semafor, an American news website.

    The US Commerce Department had been investigating whether Megaspeed was smuggling Nvidia chips into China for more than a year, according to the Financial Times.

    But tensions at the Commerce Department broke into the spotlight after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with an executive at the Singapore-based firm earlier this month.

    Politicians criticized Commerce Department Secretary Howard Lutnick for not having previously added Megaspeed to the department's so-called "Entity List" despite US intelligence warnings that the manufacturer was a possible front for smuggling sensitive AI chip technology to China.

    Huang briefly lost his job over the scandal as US officials said the woman, Alice Huang, was a Chinese spy.

    Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday, in a stunning reversal after his resignation just two weeks ago.

    The Fresh York Times reported last month that US authorities had concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset who passed information to Beijing while developing a close relationship with Jensen Huang.

    Beijing has denied those claims and called the spy accusations "groundless.".

    Nvidia shares soared more than 30% after the firm declared it reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

    Some people were happy to see him back as president of Nvidia, as videos posted to social media show.

    House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is on track to be the next speaker of the House, called the decision to reinstate Huang "indefensible, irresponsible, and incomprehensible" and vowed Congress would reinvestigate any wrongdoing by the organization and the Commerce Department.

    • A prominent singer who performed without the mandatory hijab and four members of her band and production team have been flogged by Iranian authorities, lawyers say.
    • Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were each given 74 lashes in the city of Qom, a member of their defence team told the BBC.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Parastoo Ahmadi's performance was livestreamed on her YouTube channel in December 2024.

    A prominent singer who performed without the mandatory hijab and four members of her band and production team have been flogged by Iranian authorities, lawyers say.

    Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were each given 74 lashes in the city of Qom, a member of their defence team told the BBC.

    Recent findings suggest that ahmadi, 29, wore a sleeveless dress during a concert that was livestreamed in December 2024. Iran's laws ban public performances by women and require them to wear headscarves and modest clothing.

    This June, a criminal court in Qom convicted Ahmadi and eight others of "offending public decency" through the publication of "obscene and indecent material", which they had denied.

    In addition to being sentenced to 74 lashes, they were banned from audiovisual activities and from leaving the country for two years.

    At the end of September, an appeals court in Qom rejected the defendants' appeal and confirmed the sentence, her lawyers said.

    There was widespread condemnation of the sentences from other Iranian artists and human rights activists, who warned that flogging constituted cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment, and violated the international prohibition on torture.

    On Monday, one of the defendants' lawyers told the BBC that Ahmadi and four of her male co-defendants had been flogged at the third branch of the Criminal Sentence Enforcement Office in Qom.

    "We did everything in our power to have the verdict overturned, or at least to secure a reduction in the sentence or a suspension, but it didn't work out," he stated.

    "The other lawyers and I even tried to get the enforcement of the sentence postponed, but the enforcement branch insisted on carrying it out immediately.".

    Pro-reform daily Etemad cited another defence lawyer, Mostafa Nili, as identifying the four men flogged alongside Ahmadi as Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amirali Pirnia and Mohsen Lashkari.

    "Parastoo Ahmadi's flogging for singing and dressing as she chooses is a flagrant violation of her fundamental rights and a chilling demonstration of the Iranian authorities' determination to suppress women's freedoms and to violently punish anyone who dares to challenge their discriminatory laws and policies," remarked Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI).

    Under Iranian law, which is based on the country's interpretation of Sharia, women and girls above the age of puberty must cover their hair with a hijab and wear long, loose-fitting clothing to disguise their figures.

    In 2022, protests swept across the Islamic Republic following the death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman who was detained by morality police in Tehran in September that year for allegedly wearing her hijab "improperly".

    Women burnt their headscarves or waved them in the air at the nationwide demonstrations against the clerical establishment, during which hundreds of people were killed in a crackdown by security forces.

    Industry observers note that since then, many women and girls have stopped covering their hair in public altogether in open defiance of the dress code. Authorities have responded with periodic waves of arrests, warnings, business closures and other measures.

    In January this year, thousands of people were killed and tens of thousands were arrested when security forces crushed another wave of mass anti-establishment protests, this time sparked by the country's economic crisis.

    Since the start of Iran's war with the US and Israel in late February, authorities have intensified their use of the death penalty against protesters.

    According to the Norway-based group Iran Human Rights, at least 39 men convicted over January's protests and two convicted over the 2022 unrest have been executed, along with 16 people allegedly affiliated with banned opposition groups and 17 others convicted of espionage or collaborating with foreign states.

    Another 121 protesters detained in January, including six women and five juvenile offenders, have been sentenced to death and are at imminent risk of execution, it says.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Megaspeed, the tech giant that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.

    It has been revealed that the organization will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”.

    Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the organization “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”.

    Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had debuted a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.

    TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will revision this story if it responds.

    After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the organization’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

    • Looking for a web browser without Google Chrome underneath?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, looking for a web browser without Google Chrome underneath? You can try this independent web browser now on macOS and Linux.

    Looking for a web browser without Google Chrome underneath? You can try this independent web browser now on macOS and Linux.

    Ladybird, an independent web browser with a built-from-scratch engine, is finally available for testing. On Monday, Ladybird developer Andreas Kling confirmed that the browser is launching in alpha on macOS and Linux following more than four years of development.

    It has been revealed that the release makes Ladybird the first browser in years to arrive with an entirely new engine. We’ve seen many engines emerge over time, but the most popular browsers use just three today: Gecko, Blink, and WebKit. While Gecko, now used in Mozilla Firefox, first appeared in Netscape 6 in 2000, Apple’s WebKit arrived in Safari in 2003 as a fork of KDE’s KHTML. A decade later, the Google-backed Chromium project forked WebKit to create Blink, which now powers Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Opera, and more.

    Ladybird is backed by a nonprofit organization with the goal of creating “an independent, fast and secure browser that respects user privacy and fosters an open web,” according to its website. Though Ladybird development initially began as part of a C++ project, its developers eventually began porting the code to Rust using AI.

    According to recent reports, in his post announcing the alpha, Kling notes that the browser built around the Ladybird engine “is modest but functional,” adding that “some websites won’t work” during the alpha. A Windows version of Ladybird will arrive during a “later stage” of the project.

    OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”.

    Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. After the announcement that Huang would return, Altman simply posted, “Jensen!” Many other tech CEOs have similarly refrained from commenting on the matter, given the shifting politics surrounding Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, as well as the national security concerns at the center of the controversy.

    In addition to Musk, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who served prison time for failing to stop criminal activity on the Binance crypto exchange, is also supportive of Huang.

    It has been revealed that glad to see @JensenHuang back. 👏 https://t.co/WrUjvmEyVi.

    Sources indicate that gift-giving isn’t just about grabbing something solid under a determined spending limit. It’s an expression of love, a way to show someone how well you really know them. That doesn’t mean you have to do it all on your own, though. Sometimes you just need a push in the right direction to get things rolling.

    Recent findings suggest that this year, we spent hours collecting our favorites to help you get ahead of your holiday shopping. This list has everything: minimalist smart rings, Play-Doh flowers, sleek beat machines — you name it. Whatever your needs, no matter how demanding the recipient, you’ll find something exceptional below for that special someone on your list.

    Most of us have thousands of photos in the cloud, but if a photo never makes it into the real world, did it really happen? Existentialism aside, the Cricut StickerPix offers a new way to play with photos, providing you with everything you need to turn any picture into a pro-quality print or sticker.

    If you’re a fan of Apple’s open-ear standard AirPods, the AirPods 5 are the best model yet. The higher-end pair (there are two models) offers upgraded sound, better noise cancellation, and swipe-based volume controls, bringing some Pro-level features to the buds that started the wire-free revolution.

    Sources indicate that it’s rare for a product to boast that it’s “hacker-friendly,” but the Busy Bar isn’t your average device. Equipped with a pixelated LED screen, fantastically fun buttons, and intriguing ways to play, Flipper’s open-source productivity tool breeds efficiency by, among other things, keeping coworkers from interrupting your flow with their weekend prepares.

    It has been revealed that espresso in the woods? Yes, please. The GR2’s magical mechanics make it possible, letting you turn 12 ounces of grounds into espresso without power. Its carrying case houses all the accessories needed to get that sweet shot of bean, making real coffee available virtually anywhere.

    Digital photos changed everything, but there’s still something wonderful about the visceral touch and nostalgia of analog. Fujifilm’s Instax Mini Evo provides an intriguing hybrid that bridges these worlds, with a retro design, intuitive dials and controls, and the ability to filter like it’s 1989 (or 1889?).

    Recent findings suggest that what if you could give the gift of stress-free Wi-Fi on the go? That’s the promise of TP-Link’s dual-band Roam 7, a portable Wi-Fi 7 router that simplifies connecting to public portals so travelers can connect everything to a single device and be done with it.

    For those who love travel but hate the constraints of a hotel TV, Belkin’s ConnectAir is a slick solution. Plug the transmitter into any device with a USB-C video-out port and the receiver into the TV’s HDMI port, and voilà, you’re easily (and wirelessly) connected.

    According to recent reports, the company that brought gaming to the masses still defies the odds, thanks in large part to its creative roots. Those roots run deep, and journalist Keza MacDonald’s fascinating book traces them to their source, from a simple card game company to the minds behind the biggest hits of all time.

    According to recent reports, you can give the gift of creativity with this do-it-all digital music maker. Akai’s portable sampler, beat maker, and all-around sound machine blends tactile quick keys and pads with an onboard screen so musicians can build it all in a box and send the results to their DAW of choice.

    In a recent development, for those who enjoy clever devices that just work, we give you Nimble’s “breakable” SharePower Portable Charger. The magnetically joined power bank rapidly snaps into a pair of 20W batteries, letting two people charge their phones, or works as a single 10,000mAh unit for larger top-offs.

    Upcoming Zealand artist Aldous Harding has another eccentric album on her hands with this year’s Train on the Island. The slow-burning LP is gorgeously recorded and delightfully weird, and it feels tailor-made for vinyl, making it an easy pick for Harding fans (or anyone who loves quirky indie jams).

    For those in smaller dwellings, efficient living means maximizing space. That’s where combo appliances like Ninja’s newest microwave / air fryer combo come in. The handy countertop gadget lets you zap your food, then crisp it at the end so your pizza or French fries don’t turn into a soggy mess.

    Perhaps no game in history is more anticipated than the latest entry in Rockstar’s sprawling, intricate, and absolutely bonkers open-world series. Grand Theft Auto VI is said to offer a more obsessively dense map, more realism in details like weather and passing time, and more realistic NPCs (non-player characters) than ever before. Here’s hoping those 13 years were worth the wait.

    Open-style earbuds aren’t just for the sporty; they’re an entirely different way to listen that keeps you environmentally aware without the plugged-up feeling of traditional buds. The OpenFit Pro take a balanced approach, with seamless open-ear performance and even a touch of noise reduction to dampen the din on crowded commutes.

    The old Ironman Timex was a staple for ’80s and ’90s kids, and while you can’t bring back those carefree days, remakes like the Retroware can bring back that carefree feeling. No smarts, no notifications, just a takes-a-licking Timex watch with tactile keys, 50 meters of water resistance, and totally tubular digital graphics.

    Serious gamers need a serious controller, and few take gaming more seriously than 8BitDo’s Elite-style Xbox gamepad. From its drift-proof TMR joysticks and motion support to its customizable buttons and remappable bumpers, the Ultimate 3E is the gift for that lovable control freak in your life.

    There’s regular Play-Doh for kids, but did you know that Play-Doh makes kits for adults, too? We’re not scoffing. The new Blooms sets take on Lego’s floral bouquets with more realistic-looking flower arrangements, and they include a vase. They’re equal parts nostalgic kitsch and stylish decor.

    It has been revealed that for on-the-go creators, it’s all about capturing the moment in the highest video quality possible. Insta360’s Luna Pro steadycam offers plenty of features to get the job done right, including 4K vertical video, swift file transfers, four hours of battery life, and a detachable touchscreen that doubles as a remote.

    The fresh Fitbit Air provides the same great fitness tracking we’ve come to expect in a comfortable design that virtually disappears on your wrist. Google’s AI Coach can be overly assertive, but the tracker’s great battery life and metrics for everything from sleep to blood oxygen make it an excellent gift for anyone who needs a healthy hand.

    Most mobile controllers have a serious size limit. Not Razer’s Kishi V3 Pro XL, which lets you throw a big ol’ tablet between the handles for a major visual upgrade. It also has high-quality joysticks, great grips, and customizable keys for USB-C tablets, along with haptics for Android models.

The story about three pop stars who band together to save humanity from a demonic boy band is an instant classic, with fantastic music and striking animation.

    Sources indicate that if you’re contemplating a pricey pair of sleep buds for your loved one, we urge you to halt and consider a softer (and cheaper) alternative. Piercing pillows, designed with pockets for freshly pierced ears, also work great for regular earbuds. Blissbury’s comfy and adjustable Ear Pillow is our favorite. Problem — and sleep concerns — solved.

    The Concrete Edition of Keychron’s K2 HE is not your average mechanical board. Cased in actual concrete, it offers standard keycaps to match its industrial aesthetic, both Bluetooth and 2.4GHz connectivity, and several other advanced features. This includes the ability to adjust the actuation distance of the individual Hall effect switches (hence the “HE”).

    Industry observers note that we all do it: pay a ton for a monthly streaming service for just a few series. It’s better to own the real thing, and Hacks, a hilarious drama that follows a comedian (Jean Smart) and her young writer (Hannah Einbinder) in the tumultuous “biz,” is one of HBO’s best series in years.

    Recent findings suggest that hoto’s soldering iron is super cool — and by that we mean hot, as it’s able to reach nearly 400 degrees Fahrenheit in about three seconds. The cordless, adjustable iron makes the perfect gift for your favorite DIYer, especially since it features customizable presets for virtually any job.

    Recent findings suggest that for the person on your list whose hatred for smart glasses runs deep, Knockaround’s hip, tech-free sunglasses should hit the spot. They’re available in a variety of fun styles and offer lightweight frames and polarized lenses, with both UVA and UVB shielding for attractive eye protection.

    It has been revealed that the first 3D Zelda game has been remade for the modern era. And if you fear it will diverge too much from the Nintendo 64 original, fear not: This carefully crafted remake delivers updated graphics and improved controls alongside the same stellar adventure we remember.

    Sources indicate that everyone needs a good flashlight, and perhaps your recipient’s next one should ditch the replaceable batteries. Wuben’s rechargeable G5 has a pocketable, spy-tech-inspired design, USB-C charging, and adjustable brightness. More importantly, the 400-lumen light is super compact, making it easy to stow or clip onto your bag.

    It has been revealed that if you haven’t been bombarded by the Hulken yet, it’s a rolling tote that’s blown up online. Designed to hold everything from laundry to an impromptu picnic, the durable bag is beloved for its seemingly bottomless capacity and colorful style, making it a thoughtful gift for fashionable folks on the move.

    Recent findings suggest that if a Kindle won’t quite fit into your favorite traveler’s tight pack job, consider the Xteink X4 Pro. The tiny e-reader is easy to pop into your bag or pocket thanks to its 4.3-inch display, and the latest model offers a backlit touchscreen for a more intuitive way to explore the literary world.

    In a recent development, for the coffee or tea lover in your life who’s always headed to the microwave for a heat zap, Ember’s fancy-schmancy smart mug is a luxurious way to keep things toasty. With the ability to set the temperature on the mug or in the app, the Mug 3 makes it simple to keep liquids perfectly hot indefinitely.

    Not all reusable water bottles are created equal. Give the gift of a narrow-mouthed bottle, like this 16-ounce Nalgene pick, which makes it easy to take measured sips on the go. Take this advice from someone (me) who bought the wide-mouthed version and regularly spills water all over themself.

    If your giftee is into New York City memorabilia or wants a more unique way to light up a room, this cube-shaped lamp, designed around the old MTA entrance beacons, is sure to delight. Locals will recognize the vintage symbol, which still survives in the wild, and everyone will dig the old-school vibe.

    According to recent reports, pokopia brings Pokémon to life in a cozy worldbuilding game that borrows the best from predecessors like Minecraft and Animal Crossing. The twist? The slow-burning Switch 2 title eventually rolls into an expansive adventure that lets you customize as you go.

    It has been revealed that when it comes to keeping your pet happy and healthy while you’re away, the details matter. Petkit’s most basic auto feeder offers peace of mind with dual-power protection, meal monitoring via the Petkit app, and a generous 12-cup capacity that should keep an adult cat fed for up to 15 days.

    Electronics are becoming more sustainable, and Fairphone is leading the way. The Fairphone 6 Plus may seem like a regular Android phone on paper, but the ability to repair and replace its internals, from the screen to the battery, makes it anything but average.

    Industry observers note that in many ways, the Pebble Index 01 is the gadget of our times. The stripped-back smart ring has a microphone and, with a tap of a button, records and sends your thoughts to the Pebble app over Bluetooth. You can also use it to start a timer or even add a calendar event to your phone.

    Sources indicate that sure. You could put iced tea in them, but no one’s stopping you from sipping pulpy OJ or rich chocolate milk from Kinto’s stylish glassware, which was crafted with an “uninterfering design” in mind. Needless to say, a full set makes a lovely addition to any minimalist’s ensemble.

    Industry observers note that the hippest thing in audio right now is… the hippest thing from a long time ago. Enter the modded iPod Classic from Player Mods, which refreshes Apple’s media player with some 21st-century upgrades. The 5th-gen model can be customized with several color options (including a transparent case) and up to 2TB of storage.

    For those tired of experiencing Joy-Con drift with their Nintendo Switch (or stick drift on any controller), there’s the TT Pro. Loaded with the latest anti-drift tech for joysticks and customizable triggers that let picky gamers have it their way, GuliKit’s customizable wireless controllers work with PlayStation, Nintendo, PC, iOS, and Android devices.

    Industry observers note that do you like… scary movies? That’s just one of many catchphrases that pair well with the Key Pocket, which can alter voices in real time. The tiny device sticks to the back of Apple or Android devices via magnets, granting you multiple effects for gaming, voice calls, or streaming.

    Sources indicate that pricey yet endlessly useful, this is the kind of item you might not buy for yourself, which makes it a fantastic gift. Offering a brilliantly thin yet durable framework in a stand that also hangs, pops, and never needs to come off, it’s the ultimate phone accessory.

    If someone on your list collects Game Boy, Game Boy Color, or Game Boy Advance cartridges, the GB Operator might be the perfect gift. The slick, transparent USB-C device makes it easy to play and manage classic titles on a macOS or Windows machine via emulation, with or without achievements.

    According to recent reports, dock & Bay’s blankets are a great choice for almost everyone. They provide a soft space on which to relax or entertain, whether at the park or on your hardwood floors at home, and they’re incredibly easy to pack. Plus, they have a water-resistant bottom and come in an array of fun colors.

    This radical upgrade of the middle child in Sonos’ soundbar lineup may be the best (little) soundbar you can buy. It delivers musical sound, surprisingly full and cinematic bass, and brain-tricking immersion thanks to drivers that now point every which way; it can also expand or connect with other Sonos speakers and stream almost anything.

    The Pocket Scion is unlike any musical instrument you’ve witnessed before, one that uses the “biofeedback” from plants to trigger built-in synths. The device offers MIDI-out to send digital signals to outboard synths, and it includes an app for both macOS and Windows, finally giving you a way to make your favorite fern a rockstar.

    Your favorite gamer needs an awesome monitor, but there are 10 billion options. Alienware’s 34-inch Penta Tandem QD-OLED delivers top-end picture quality, with vibrant colors and perfect blacks, plus a swift 280Hz refresh rate. Best of all, it’s not nearly as expensive as you might think.

    Few devices evoke more sheer nostalgic joy than Sony’s OG PlayStation console from ’94. If you know a gamer, Lego’s latest replica brings it all flooding back with several brick-ified details, including a pop-up hinge, a gamepad, and a number of hidden surprises waiting to be discovered.

    Industry observers note that nothing can replace our furry friends, so for pets that tend to wander, only the best tracking tech will do. Enter the Fi Ultra, which uses Starlink technology via T-Mobile to track pets almost anywhere, even in cellular dead zones.

    In a recent development, if your favorite cinephile is looking to get off the streaming carousel, the Kaleidescape Strato E is the key. The premium player lets library builders locally store and play their favorite films and TV reveals in lossless 4K resolution with Dolby Atmos for sterling entertainment that’s all theirs.

    If there’s someone on your list who loves plants but can’t seem to take care of them, the Gardyn Studio 2 can bring life to their living room. The smart hydroponic garden is easy to set up and features automated, AI-powered lighting, helping anyone maintain a green thumb.

    You create a home for your pets; they create a mess for your home. It’s the circle of life (or carpet, anyway). Thankfully, Bissell’s pro-grade cleaner uses a concentrated stream of formula and 12 rows of rotating brushes to do the dirty work for you, keeping your carpets in good order.

    Recent findings suggest that have you broken something fragile that seems impossible to mend? Maybe all you need is a Kintsugi Repair Kit, which provides the Japanese method and a special lacquer to repair and restore broken ceramics to good health. The resulting golden scar is merely to remind us that rebuilding is possible.

    Soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for way less than Apple’s latest AirPods Pro.

    It’s time for a smarter robovac. Thankfully, there’s the Matic, which looks less like the rambling discs that pervade the space and more like an actual robot that, well, vacuums. It doesn’t get under beds, but it also doesn’t get stuck under them, and it does a great job providing truly no-fuss cleaning thanks to its superb mapping.

    Recent findings suggest that there’s no shortage of mobile gaming controllers, but few are as stealthy or as compact as the MCON. The sliding gamepad quickly attaches to any MagSafe- or Pixelsnap-ready phone, letting you game with a set of satisfying controls that feel more natural than most rivals.

    Recent findings suggest that it can be hard to keep in touch with friends, but Big Walk might be the game that gets the gang back together. The cooperative multiplayer title drops players into a wacky world as spherical humanoids who must solve puzzles by chatting and teaming up. You’ll want at least two copies, and sessions support up to 12 players.

The Viture Pro 2 are a slick pair of augmented-reality shades with speakers, micro-OLED screens, and a bonus feature: diopter-adjusting dials, which can sharpen the focus of whatever they’re mirroring from a phone or other device over a USB-C tether. Fancy!

    According to recent reports, the BYOK (Bring Your Own Keyboard) is a distraction-free way for creatives to get their thoughts down without the allure of silly YouTube videos or notifications about their dog’s flea meds. No frills, just a low-resolution LCD screen that works with most keyboards and provides plenty of power for the long haul.

    The Switch 2 leverages the same ideas as its predecessor, only with a larger, 7.9-inch display, a faster chip, and a bevy of new social features. However, its most vital trait is that it’s the newest Nintendo console, which means access to a host of weird, beautiful, family-friendly games that only Nintendo could dream up, now on a better screen.

    It has been revealed that wiiM is a popular Sonos alternative, thanks in part to excellent software that works across its multiple streaming amplifiers and other products. The WiiM Sound is the brand’s sharpest smart speaker, with accessible controls, Alexa and Google smarts, and the ability to connect to other WiiM gear in surround sound or throughout your home.

    Recent findings suggest that when it comes to jotting down notes, there’s nothing like the pen and paper. At least, that’s what we thought before we tried the Remarkable Paper Pure. Offering a strikingly realistic writing experience that saves everything in the digital realm, this tablet is a brilliant way to bridge the gap and save paper.

    Once The Great British Baking Show becomes an obsession, only a serious stand mixer will do for replicating recipes at home. This mixer’s timeless design adds new features in what KitchenAid calls its biggest upgrade since 1955, with a new half-speed setting and a control lever that lets you set speeds between its standard settings.

    Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded.

    Industry observers note that multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

    It has been revealed that coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

    Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1119 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself?
    • Now, the tech giant has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business.
    • Michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.

    Now, the tech giant has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman, who’s currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.

    Michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April.

    “We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano said. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the manufacturer day to day.

    In a recent development, the team includes co-founders Lincoln Murr (CEO) and John Peterson (CTO). Both joined from Coinbase, where, Mignano notes, they were the heads of AI product and engineering, leading rolls out like Coinbase advisor, Coinbase for agents, agentic wallets, and others.

    The startup arrives as AI continues to make inroads into financial services, but allowing AI to take over people’s actual investments requires a latest level of trust. Supertake is betting that people will ultimately be willing to take that leap, given recent improvements in frontier AI models.

    Right now, Supertake works with Coinbase and Robinhood, and the firm intends to expand to more brokerages over time. The idea is that you can explain, in broad, natural language, what you believe about how the world is going to change, and Supertake’s AI will iterate with you back and forth to turn that idea into a “take” that’s investable.

    Under the hood, the startup is leveraging frontier AI technology and tools, combined with its own proprietary software that directs and limits what the AI can do.

    It has been revealed that supertake’s users’ ideas are tracked on a leaderboard on the site, so others who agree can invest alongside them. For instance, there’s currently an idea on the leaderboard about looksmaxxing and longevity becoming more of a trend, where the portfolio includes certain pharma and cosmetic companies that could potentially benefit.

    For now, these portfolios consist of stock picks, but the team wants to expand the service over time to handle other types of transactions, like shorts, derivatives, perpetuals, long exposure, or even prediction markets — the latter handled through partnerships with companies in that space.

    Despite these “takes” seeming like bets on what could happen next in a given market, Murr stresses that this doesn’t make Supertake itself a prediction market.

    It has been revealed that “We think it’s a novel and very much improved way to create what was previously considered the robo-advisor experience,” he says. “When that came out, it had this amazing vision and direction of allowing people to have digital asset management. We think now is actually the time for that, with AI agents being so widely proliferated.”.

    According to recent reports, “I don’t think this is necessarily a prediction market by any means. The idea of natural language translation into an underlying set of assets feels different in that regard,” he claims.

    Still, the startup could wade into short-term predictions if a user’s take involves something they believe could happen in the near future, like who might win an election.

    In a recent development, “We’re primarily focused on the longer, medium-term holdings today. But that being remarked, we don’t want to preclude people from building out very hyper short-term strategies that might exist,” Murr adds.

    To address people’s concerns over AI managing their money, Supertake’s team says it’s implementing certain guardrails and spend limits. For instance, the AI has no ability to deposit or withdraw funds on a user’s behalf without their explicit consent. There are also drift limits in place so the portfolio stays balanced, plus allow and deny lists (meaning which assets the AI may and may not trade), real-time monitoring for anomalous activity, tools to set trade size limits, and a restriction that keeps agents from seeing the user’s brokerage credentials.

    In a recent development, “We view it as somewhat analogous to self-driving cars, actually, where there is a spectrum here of both trust and technological innovations that are happening,” indicates Murr. “Where a few years ago you may not feel comfortable getting in a car that has lane assist, but today you get in a Waymo, and it’s like nothing. And we think that there’s a very similar progression happening with the agentic finance space, and we’re far further along in the technological spectrum than people think.”.

    Sources indicate that access to Supertake is still behind a waitlist while in beta, but the founders mentioned they’ve put their money where their mouths are. Murr and Peterson are letting it manage “tens of thousands” and “thousands” of dollars, respectively.

    Mignano, meanwhile, states he has Supertake managing “hundreds of thousands” of dollars.

    According to recent reports, with the new funding, which follows a $2 million pre-seed round, Supertake aims to expand its team in areas like engineering, design, growth marketing, and others. Mignano and Murr are in New York, while Peterson is in the Austin area but commutes to New York at times. The team says it hopes to figure out a hybrid work model as it grows.

    What strike on Russian ship in Libya indicates about spread of Ukraine war

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack.
    • The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi, co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders?
    • The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack. It wasn't.

    The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi, co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders?

    The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading. But this attack, which Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called "an exemplary operation" will inevitably raise the stakes another notch.

    Russia, which is right now engaged in a non-stop campaign to batter Ukraine's civilian population into submission with daily missile and drone strikes, has called it "a dangerous escalation".

    It follows the suspected Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin described as an act of terrorism.

    Ukraine's long-range drones have also previously struck Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga.

    Some of Ukraine's more audacious long-range drone attacks â what Zelensky likes to call "long-range sanctions" â have also struck targets thousands of kilometres beyond Ukraine's borders with Russia, deep inside Siberia.

    The most notable of these was last year's Operation Spider's Web, which involved a specially adapted lorry that drove close to a Russian strategic nuclear bomber airbase and released a "swarm" of explosive drones that damaged or destroyed several expensive bombers.

    And Ukraine has also been active further south in Africa where its forces have targeted Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps, the successor to the infamous Wagner Group that was accused of carrying out numerous human rights abuses.

    It's not just Russia that will be alarmed by this latest Ukrainian operation in Benghazi harbour. The United Nations mission in Libya has already expressed its "deep concern".

    Libyan officials point out that their country is not a party to the Russia-Ukraine war, although the Merkury and an accompanying cargo ship that was also hit were berthed in the eastern part of Libya controlled by the pro-Moscow warlord and self-styled "Field Marshal" Khalifa Haftar.

    How Ukraine drone attacks on Russian ships unfolded.

    Throughout this year the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) has condemned all attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and today the global shipping community will be wondering whether this attack does indeed set a dangerous precedent.

    If Ukraine can proposal and execute such a bold attack on Russian ships in a nominally neutral harbour so far from home, where does this stop?

    As the fifth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches, this war has already been spreading, notably in other parts of Europe.

    On Friday, several Russian projectiles landed well inside Poland's borders, just 60 miles from an Anglo-French exercise of forces intended to be deployed following an eventual ceasefire in Ukraine.

    This, stated Poland's PM Donald Tusk, was "a deliberate provocation" by Moscow.

    It's not the first time Russian munitions have landed inside Poland, and therefore inside Nato territory, but observers have pointed out that Russia's probing of Nato's borders is becoming ever more brazen and some are calling for a firmer response.

    But Russia is already heavily sanctioned by the West, with Europe having reduced much â but not all â of its energy imports from Russia, so the options for retaliation are limited, short of military confrontation, which no one wants.

    Watch: CCTV shows explosion after Poland notes airspace violated by Russian missile.

    Both Romania and Moldova have found themselves frequently struck by overflying Russian drones targeting Ukraine's Black Sea ports, while Bulgaria and Romania have suffered maritime drone attacks on commercial shipping just offshore in the Black Sea.

    In the case of Romania, a Nato member, fast jets have had to be scrambled to intercept incoming Russian drones and there is a profound suspicion that these incursions are not all accidental.

    The three Baltic states â Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania â all have borders with Russia and all consider themselves right on the front lines in this war.

    There have been a number of anonymous attacks on military industrial facilities in these countries, blamed on agents acting on Moscow's behalf.

    Russia, for its part, suspects Estonia of being complicit in Ukrainian drone attacks on the Baltic involving overflights through Estonian airspace.

    Hybrid warfare isn't upcoming but it is on the rise.

    It refers to the practice, by either side, of carrying out largely anonymous and unattributable operations using methods like cyber attacks, the burning down of warehouses supplying military equipment and the dispatching of drones, both for surveillance and loaded with explosives.

    This autumn, Germany's Leipzig-Halle airport, which is used as a resupply hub by Ukraine's cargo aircraft, was targeted by three explosive drones that were discovered before anyone was hurt.

    Sources indicate that there have been other incidents involving explosive packages sent across Europe targeting Germany, Poland and the UK. Moscow denies any involvement.
